reason: 'Jordan put three carrot seeds in a deep hole.' Carrot seeds are tiny and must be sown shallow (about 1 cm deep); planted in a deep hole they usually do not come up.
'Cat and hat sound the same!' (uncorrected) Rhyming words are not the same sound; they end with the same sound, which the story never says.
'Felix tapped higher sounds' / 'He tapped the wrong spot. The sound was too low.' A single small bell makes one pitch; tapping a different spot on it does not play higher or lower notes.
'One monkey was alone on the floor.' Two monkeys had been bumped off the bed (five to four to three), so two were on the floor.
'Then she came to the K.' Audrey's name is spelled A-U-D-R-E-Y, as the story itself says, and has no K.
'The pencil marks shined, wet and new. "Wait for them to dry," said Grandma.' Pencil marks are dry graphite; they are not wet and do not need to dry.

At school nap time, 'The sky was black' and then it gets light and Lily shouts 'It's morning!' with the teacher agreeing. School nap time is during the day, so the sky is not night-dark and morning does not dawn then.
'A small green frog sat there' in the snow. Frogs hibernate in winter and are not out sitting in the snow.

Nia: 'It is not morning now. We ate breakfast before, and now it is play time,' left uncorrected. Morning does not end when breakfast is over; they went to the park right after breakfast, so it was still morning.
'It will make your tooth happy,' Grandma said, giving a sweet. Sweets are bad for teeth; they can cause cavities.
'It had three pointy sides.' A triangle has three straight sides and three pointy corners; the sides are not pointy.
'Its little wheels were still spinning.' A toy car left long before would have stopped rolling; its wheels would not still be spinning.
